items.title: Social and local presence
items.source: Draft for review. Written by an AI assistant from general UK small-business knowledge, not from a cited document. Check every fact against current GOV.UK and regulator guidance, and have someone who does this work review it, before it is activated. Rules differ by country and change.
items.body: People often look for a business online before they visit or buy. Claim your listing on map and search services, and keep your name, address, opening hours, phone and photos accurate. Choose one or two social platforms where your customers actually are, rather than all of them, and post regularly at a pace you can keep. Show real people, products and results, answer messages and comments promptly, and thank people for reviews. Take part in local groups and community events. Check what people say about you and keep things consistent everywhere. Being easy to find and trust matters more than posting often.

questions.prompt: What should you keep accurate on online business listings?

options.text: Name, address, opening hours, phone number and photos

questions.prompt: How many social platforms should a small business start with?

options.text: One or two where its customers actually are
As many as possible at any cost

questions.prompt: Why answer messages and comments promptly?

options.text: It shows customers that you are reliable and helps sales

questions.prompt: Which matters most for a local business online?

options.text: Being easy to find and trust
